# Installing Godot 4.3 Standard

Before writing a single line of Kadi code, let's get **Godot 4.3** running on your machine. Download it directly from the official site ([godotengine.org](https://godotengine.org)).

On the download page you will see two editions:
- **Godot 4.3 Standard** (includes GDScript — **choose this one!**)
- **Godot 4.3 .NET** (adds C# support, requires external .NET SDK)

Because our entire Kadi game is written in [[GDScript]], the **Standard** edition is smaller, faster to launch, and needs zero external SDKs to run on Windows, macOS, Linux, or Android.

```gdscript
# Once Godot is open, this 4-line script is all it takes to verify your setup:
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
    print("Godot 4.3 ready — time to build Kadi!")
```

> [!GODOT]
> Godot does not have an installer wizard! The downloaded `.zip` contains the entire engine in one portable executable file. Unzip it anywhere (such as `Documents/Godot/`), double-click the executable, and the **Project Manager** window opens immediately.

> [!WHY]
> Why lock onto **Godot 4.3** specifically? Because Godot 4 replaced Godot 3's old APIs (`instance()` became `instantiate()`, `onready var` became `@onready var`, `connect("pressed", self, ...)` became `button.pressed.connect(...)`). Using Godot 4.3 guarantees that every snippet in this companion app works on the first try without version confusion.

## How This Lesson Fits Into the Full Kadi Game

| Question | Answer for This Lesson |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Which Phase & Step?** | Phase 1 (Project Setup & Deck Model) — Lesson 1: *Installing Godot 4.3 Standard* |
| **Which File Do I Edit?** | `Godot_v4.3-stable (Portable Executable)` |
| **Scene / Node Context** | `root (Viewport)  (Godot Runtime SceneTree)` |
| **What Problem Does It Solve?** | Godot 4.3 Standard includes full GDScript support in a single ~100 MB portable executable with zero installation wizard. |

### Detailed Explanation of Each Godot Editor Action

1. **Open godotengine.org/download in your browser.** — Configures `Godot_v4.3-stable (Portable Executable)` in the Godot 4.3 Editor so the scene hierarchy and script references stay in sync at runtime.
2. Download **Godot 4.3 Standard** (NOT the .NET version — Kadi uses pure GDScript). — Configures `Godot_v4.3-stable (Portable Executable)` in the Godot 4.3 Editor so the scene hierarchy and script references stay in sync at runtime.
3. **Extract the downloaded `.zip` archive to a folder on your computer (e.g. `Desktop/Godot/`).** — Configures `Godot_v4.3-stable (Portable Executable)` in the Godot 4.3 Editor so the scene hierarchy and script references stay in sync at runtime.
4. Double-click the extracted Godot executable to open the **Godot Project Manager** window. — Configures `Godot_v4.3-stable (Portable Executable)` in the Godot 4.3 Editor so the scene hierarchy and script references stay in sync at runtime.


## Deep-Dive Walkthrough: How Installing Godot 4.3 Standard Works Under the Hood

When beginners build a card game in **Godot 4.3**, one of the hardest parts is picturing what happens **in memory** between the moment a player clicks a card on screen and the moment the game state updates. Let's trace `Godot_v4.3-stable (Portable Executable)` step by step at a real 4-player Kadi table:

- **Core Principle 1**: Godot 4.3 Standard includes full GDScript support in a single ~100 MB portable executable with zero installation wizard.
- **Core Principle 2**: Pinning version 4.3 ensures every node property, signal syntax, and `@onready` annotation in this course matches your editor 100%.

### Answering the "Why?" Questions Beginners Ask Most

| Common Question While Coding This Step | Clear Answer & Rulebook Rationale |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Which Godot 4.3 edition should you download for this Kadi tutorial, and why?** | **Standard edition, because Kadi is built 100% in GDScript and needs no external .NET SDK** — The Standard edition has GDScript built right in with zero extra dependencies. |
| **How is Godot 4.3 installed after downloading the `.zip` archive?** | **Simply extract the `.zip` and double-click the portable executable** — Godot is a self-contained portable executable — unzipping the file is the entire installation. |
| **What is the very first window that appears when you launch the Godot executable?** | **The Project Manager (where you create or open a project)** — Godot opens to the Project Manager first; once you create or select a project, the full editor opens. |

- **Scenario / Goal**: Write a `_ready()` function that prints `"Godot 4.3 ready!"` to the Output panel.
- **How Godot Evaluates It**: When your script runs `extends Node`, Godot executes each line top-to-bottom on the active scene or resource instance, validating types and updating the live Kadi state.

# Creating the Kadi Project & Organizing `res://`

One of the biggest reasons beginners get lost halfway through building a game is not knowing *where* each new script or scene file should be saved. We are going to solve that right now by creating a clean, permanent folder layout inside `res://`.

### Step 1: Create the Project
In the Project Manager, click **New Project**, name it `Kadi`, click **Create Folder**, choose the **Compatibility** renderer, and click **Create & Edit**.

### Step 2: Create Our Folder Layout in the FileSystem Dock
Look at the **FileSystem dock** in the bottom-left corner of the Godot editor. Right-click `res://` and select **Create New → Folder** to create this exact structure:

```text
res://
├── scripts/          # Pure GDScript files (CardTypes, CardData, GameState, TurnManager, RuleValidator)
├── scenes/
│   ├── card/         # CardScene.tscn + card_scene.gd
│   ├── table/        # Table.tscn + table.gd (Main game board)
│   └── ui/           # DeclareSuitDialog.tscn + declare_suit_dialog.gd
├── assets/           # Downloaded 2D card packs (assets/cards/), table felt & UI
└── audio/            # Downloaded sound effects (.ogg / .wav)
```

> [!GODOT]
> At the very top center of the Godot window, you will see workspace switcher buttons: **2D**, **3D**, **Script**, and **AssetLib**. Because Kadi is a 2D card game, click **2D** now so you are looking at the 2D canvas (outlined by a thin purple/blue rectangle representing the 1152×648 game window).

> [!WHY]
> Why choose the **Compatibility** renderer over **Forward+**? Forward+ is built for heavy 3D desktop lighting. Compatibility uses OpenGL ES 3, which starts up faster, runs smoothly on any laptop or budget Android phone, and exports cleanly to HTML5 Web builds!

## How This Lesson Fits Into the Full Kadi Game

| Question | Answer for This Lesson |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Which Phase & Step?** | Phase 1 (Project Setup & Deck Model) — Lesson 2: *Creating the Kadi Project & Folder Structure* |
| **Which File Do I Edit?** | `res://project.godot` |
| **Scene / Node Context** | `res:// (FileSystem Dock — Create these folders now!)` |
| **What Problem Does It Solve?** | Every file path in Godot starts with `res://`, which points to your project's root folder. |

### Detailed Explanation of Each Godot Editor Action

1. In the Project Manager, click **+ New** (or **New Project**). — Configures `res://project.godot` in the Godot 4.3 Editor so the scene hierarchy and script references stay in sync at runtime.
2. Set Project Name to `Kadi`, click **Create Folder**, and select the **Compatibility** renderer. Click **Create & Edit**. — Configures `res://project.godot` in the Godot 4.3 Editor so the scene hierarchy and script references stay in sync at runtime.
3. In the **FileSystem dock** (bottom-left), right-click `res://` -> **Create New -> Folder** and create `scripts`, `scenes`, and `audio`. — Organizes your `res://` project folders (`scripts/`, `scenes/`, `assets/cards/`, `assets/audio/`) so Godot tracks every resource UID.
4. Right-click `res://scenes` -> **Create New -> Folder** and create three subfolders: `card`, `table`, and `ui`. — Configures `res://project.godot` in the Godot 4.3 Editor so the scene hierarchy and script references stay in sync at runtime.
5. Locate the 5 key editor areas: **Scene dock** (top-left), **FileSystem dock** (bottom-left), **Main Viewport** (center, switch to **2D** at the top), **Inspector** (right), and **Output / Debugger** (bottom bar). — Organizes your `res://` project folders (`scripts/`, `scenes/`, `assets/cards/`, `assets/audio/`) so Godot tracks every resource UID.


## Deep-Dive Walkthrough: How Creating the Kadi Project & Folder Structure Works Under the Hood

When beginners build a card game in **Godot 4.3**, one of the hardest parts is picturing what happens **in memory** between the moment a player clicks a card on screen and the moment the game state updates. Let's trace `res://project.godot` step by step at a real 4-player Kadi table:

- **Core Principle 1**: Every file path in Godot starts with `res://`, which points to your project's root folder.
- **Core Principle 2**: Creating `res://scripts/` and `res://scenes/` upfront prevents a messy project root as we add cards, popups, and table scripts.
- **Core Principle 3**: `F5` runs the main project scene; `F6` runs whichever scene tab is currently open in the editor.

### Answering the "Why?" Questions Beginners Ask Most

| Common Question While Coding This Step | Clear Answer & Rulebook Rationale |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Which dock in the Godot 4.3 editor shows your project's folders (`res://scripts/`, `res://scenes/`)?** | **The FileSystem dock (bottom-left)** — The FileSystem dock in the bottom-left displays all files and folders on disk rooted at `res://`. |
| **Where does text from `print()` appear when you run your game with `F5`?** | **In the Output tab of the Bottom Panel** — The Output tab along the bottom panel displays all `print()` output and engine messages. |
| **What is the difference between pressing `F5` and pressing `F6` in Godot?** | **F5 runs the project's Main Scene; F6 runs only the currently open scene tab** — `F5` launches the whole game starting from the configured Main Scene, while `F6` is a handy shortcut to test just the currently open scene in isolation. |

### Concrete Example: Tracing Input → Execution → Output

- **Scenario / Goal**: Define a constant `CARD_SCENE_PATH` of type `String` set to `"res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn"`.
- **How Godot Evaluates It**: When your script runs `const CARD_SCENE_PATH: String = "res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn"`, Godot executes each line top-to-bottom on the active scene or resource instance, validating types and updating the live Kadi state.
- **Expected Runtime Behavior**: A compile-time constant pointing to our CardScene file in res://scenes/card/.

Every single line in the snippet has a specific job. Use this table to trace exactly what Godot does from top to bottom:

| Line | GDScript Code | Exact Meaning & Why It's Written This Way |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Line 1** | `# Every file in our project has a predictable res:// address:` | Inline comment documenting: *Every file in our project has a predictable res:// address:* (ignored by GDScript at runtime). |
| **Line 2** | `const CARD_SCENE_PATH: String = "res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn"` | Defines compile-time constant `CARD_SCENE_PATH` (`String`) = `"res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn"` so magic values aren't scattered in code. |
| **Line 3** | `const TABLE_SCENE_PATH: String = "res://scenes/table/table.tscn"` | Defines compile-time constant `TABLE_SCENE_PATH` (`String`) = `"res://scenes/table/table.tscn"` so magic values aren't scattered in code. |
| **Line 4** | `const SUIT_DIALOG_PATH: String = "res://scenes/ui/declare_suit_dialog.tscn"` | Defines compile-time constant `SUIT_DIALOG_PATH` (`String`) = `"res://scenes/ui/declare_suit_dialog.tscn"` so magic values aren't scattered in code. |

# Building `res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn`

In Godot, you never create 54 card nodes by hand. Instead, you design **one** reusable card template scene — `res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn` — and stamp out copies from code using `[[PackedScene]].instantiate()`.

> [!GODOT]
> Why make the root node of `card_scene.tscn` a `[[Control]]` instead of a `Node2D`? Because in Godot 4, `Control` nodes can be dropped directly into an `HBoxContainer` (Horizontal Box Container), which automatically spaces, centers, and reflows the player's hand whenever cards are drawn or played! Simply set `Card`'s **Layout → Custom Minimum Size** to `84 × 120` pixels.

Here is how we spawn a card from `card_scene.tscn` in GDScript:

```gdscript
const CardScene: PackedScene = preload("res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn")

func spawn_card(card_data: CardData, parent_node: Node) -> Control:
    var card_node: Control = CardScene.instantiate()
    parent_node.add_child(card_node)  # 1. Add to SceneTree FIRST
    card_node.setup(card_data)        # 2. Populate labels SECOND
    return card_node
```

> [!MISTAKE]
> Always call `parent_node.add_child(card_node)` **BEFORE** calling `card_node.setup(card_data)`! Why? Because `@onready` variables inside `card_scene.gd` (`$TopRankLabel`, `$CenterSuitLabel`) are only initialized when `card_node` enters the SceneTree via `add_child()`.

> [!WHY]
> Making `Card` extend `Control` with `custom_minimum_size = Vector2(84, 120)` lets Godot's `HBoxContainer` automatically space and fan out the player's hand!

| :--- | :--- |
| **Which Phase & Step?** | Phase 1 (Tangible Quickstart: Visual Card Scene & Playable Table) — Lesson 3: *Building the Visual `CardScene.tscn` Template* |
| **Which File Do I Edit?** | `res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn` |
| **Scene / Node Context** | `Card (Control)  (custom_minimum_size = Vector2(84, 120))` |

### Detailed Explanation of Each Godot Editor Action

1. In the top menu, click **Scene -> New Scene**. — Creates an empty scene workspace in Godot 4.3 so you can assemble a self-contained `.tscn` node hierarchy.
2. In the Scene dock, click **User Interface (Control)** as the root node, and rename `Control` to `Card`. — Uses a `Control` root node so this UI element participates in Godot's container layout, anchor presets, and touch/mouse routing.
3. With `Card` selected, go to the **Inspector** (right) -> **Layout -> Transform -> Custom Minimum Size** and set `x = 84`, `y = 120`. — Reserves a fixed minimum bounding box (`Vector2`) so parent `HBoxContainer` or `VBoxContainer` nodes never collapse this control to `0×0` pixels.
4. ## Deep-Dive Walkthrough: How Building the Visual CardScene.tscn Template Works Under the Hood

When beginners build a card game in **Godot 4.3**, one of the hardest parts is picturing what happens **in memory** between the moment a player clicks a card on screen and the moment the game state updates. Let's trace `res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn` step by step at a real 4-player Kadi table:

- **Core Principle 1**: Making `Card` extend `Control` with `custom_minimum_size = Vector2(84, 120)` lets Godot's `HBoxContainer` automatically space and fan out the player's hand!
- **Core Principle 2**: An invisible `ClickButton` (`flat = true`) covering the card gives us instant mouse, touch, and keyboard focus support via `ClickButton.pressed`.
- **Core Principle 3**: We build `card_scene.tscn` ONCE in the editor and stamp out copies at runtime using `preload(...).instantiate()`.

### Answering the "Why?" Questions Beginners Ask Most

| Common Question While Coding This Step | Clear Answer & Rulebook Rationale |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Why did we choose `Control` (with `custom_minimum_size = Vector2(84, 120)`) as the root node of `card_scene.tscn`?** | **So `CardScene` instances automatically lay out and reflow inside an `HBoxContainer` hand** — Godot's `Container` nodes (like `HBoxContainer`) automatically position and space `Control` children based on their `custom_minimum_size`. |
| **What does `CardScene.instantiate()` return?** | **A brand-new Node tree cloned from `card_scene.tscn` ready to be added with `add_child()`** — `instantiate()` clones the `PackedScene` template into a live Node hierarchy. |
| **Why do we add a flat `ClickButton` child covering `CardScene`?** | **To detect mouse clicks and screen taps cleanly via `ClickButton.pressed` without writing manual bounding-box math** — A flat `Button` covering the card gives reliable click and touch events out of the box via its `pressed` signal. |

# Making Your Card Come Alive When Clicked (`res://scenes/card/card_scene.gd`)

> [!TIP]
> **Tangible Milestone:** In the next 3 minutes, you will attach a script to `CardScene.tscn`, press **F6**, and **click your playing card in the game window to watch it physically pop up `-14px` and back down**!

Now let's attach a script to our `Card` root node in `res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn` so each card can:
1. Work **immediately on its own** when you press **F6** (even before we build the 54-card deck in Phase 2!) AND automatically upgrade to display full `CardData` resources or downloaded PNG sprites from `res://assets/cards/`.
2. Visually **lift up by 14 pixels** (`position.y = -14.0`) whenever it is selected in your hand.
3. Emit a custom `card_clicked(card_node: Control)` [[Signals|signal]] whenever the player clicks or taps the card!

## 1. Caching Child Nodes with `@onready`

Instead of calling `get_node("TopRankLabel")` every time a card updates, we use Godot 4's `[[@onready]]` annotation together with the `$NodePath` shorthand:

```gdscript
@onready var card_bg: Panel = $CardBg
@onready var card_art: TextureRect = $CardArt
@onready var top_rank_label: Label = $TopRankLabel
@onready var center_suit_label: Label = $CenterSuitLabel
@onready var click_button: Button = $ClickButton
```

> [!MISTAKE]
> **Why `@onready` Matters:** If you write `var top_rank_label: Label = $TopRankLabel` *without* `@onready`, Godot runs that line the instant `.instantiate()` is called — *before* the child `Label` nodes have entered the Scene Tree — so `$TopRankLabel` evaluates to `null`! Adding `@onready` tells Godot: *"Wait until `_ready()` when all child nodes exist."*

## 2. The "Call Down, Signal Up" Golden Rule of Godot

How should `CardScene` tell `Table.tscn` that the player just tapped this card?
- **Never** write `get_parent().get_parent().on_card_clicked(self)` inside `card_scene.gd`! That couples your card to one exact parent hierarchy and breaks as soon as you test `card_scene.tscn` alone with **F6**.
- Instead, follow Godot's golden rule: **Call Down, Signal Up**:
  - **Call Down**: The parent (`Table`) calls methods down on its child (`card_node.setup(...)`, `card_node.set_selected(true)`).
  - **Signal Up**: The child (`CardScene`) emits `card_clicked.emit(self)` upward without caring who is listening!

| Communication Direction | How to Write It in Godot 4.3 | Kadi Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Parent ➔ Child (Call Down)** | Direct method call on `@onready` or instanced child | `card_node.set_selected(true)` |
| **Child ➔ Parent (Signal Up)** | Declare `signal` in child; parent calls `.connect()` | `card_clicked.emit(self)` |

## 3. Instant Click-to-Lift Testing with **F6**

Notice in `_on_click_button_pressed()` below: if `card_clicked.get_connections().is_empty()` is `true` (meaning you pressed **F6** to test `card_scene.tscn` by itself with no `Table` parent attached), clicking the card automatically toggles `set_selected(not is_selected)` so you can test the `-14px` lift animation immediately!

## Line-by-Line Code Walkthrough

| Line | GDScript Code | Exact Meaning & Why It's Written This Way |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Line 2** | `extends Control` | Matches the `Control` root node of `card_scene.tscn`. |
| **Line 4** | `signal card_clicked(card_node: Control)` | Declares a custom typed signal that passes the clicked card node to any listener (`Table.gd`). |
| **Line 6–10** | `@onready var card_bg: Panel = $CardBg` | Caches child node references safely when `_ready()` runs. |
| **Line 16** | `click_button.pressed.connect(_on_click_button_pressed)` | Wires the invisible full-rect `Button`'s built-in `pressed` signal to our handler function. |
| **Line 25** | `func set_selected(selected: bool) -> void:` | Public method called by `Table.gd` (or standalone F6 test) to lift or drop the card visually. |
| **Line 27** | `var lift: float = -14.0 if is_selected else 0.0` | Ternary expression: `-14.0` pixels (upward in 2D) when selected, `0.0` when deselected. |

# Building `Table.tscn` & Fanning Your First Hand on Screen!

> [!TIP]
> **Tangible Milestone:** Right now in Phase 1, you will assemble the main `Table.tscn` game board, press **F5**, and see a **green felt Kadi tabletop with a center discard card and 4 clickable cards fanned in your hand**!

Everything you see in Godot is a [[Node]] arranged in a scene tree. By combining the `CardScene.tscn` template you just built with an [[HBoxContainer]] (`PlayerHandContainer`) on `Table.tscn`, Godot automatically spaces and centers your player's hand across the bottom of the screen!

## 1. Architecting the Main `Table.tscn` Scene Tree

When building any 2D game in Godot 4.3, we separate **World / Board Nodes** (`Node2D` / `Control` on the table) from **Heads-Up Display (HUD) Nodes** (wrapped inside a `[[CanvasLayer]]` so buttons and status labels stay pinned to the screen even if a camera moves or shakes):

| Node in `Table.tscn` | Godot Class | Role on the Kadi Table |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`Table`** | `Node2D` | Root node of the main scene (`res://scenes/table/table.tscn`) with `table.gd` attached. |
| **`Background`** | `ColorRect` | Renders the deep emerald felt tabletop (`#0E231C`, `1152×648`). |
| **`DiscardSlot`** | `Control` | Center slot (`534, 220`) holding the active face-up discard card. |
| **`PlayerHandContainer`** | `HBoxContainer` | Automatically fans and spaces Player 0's `CardScene` instances horizontally (`separation = 10`). |
| **`HUD`** | `CanvasLayer` | Top UI overlay holding `StatusLabel`, `FeedbackLabel`, `PlaySelectedButton`, `DrawButton`, and `NikoKadiButton`. |

## 2. How `Table.gd` Spawns Cards into `PlayerHandContainer`

We preload `res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn` as a `[[PackedScene]]` constant and call `CardScene.instantiate()` inside a `for` loop to stamp out 4 cards in your hand and 1 face-up starter card in `DiscardSlot`:

```gdscript
const CardScene: PackedScene = preload("res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn")

func spawn_card_on_table(parent: Node, rank_text: String, suit_text: String, is_red: bool) -> Control:
    var card_node: Control = CardScene.instantiate()
    parent.add_child(card_node) # 1. Add to SceneTree FIRST so @onready nodes exist!
    card_node.setup_preview(rank_text, suit_text, is_red) # 2. Configure visuals SECOND!
    return card_node
```

> [!GODOT]
> **Always `add_child()` Before Configuring a Node:** Notice how we call `parent.add_child(card_node)` *before* calling `setup_preview()`. That guarantees all `@onready` child nodes inside `card_scene.gd` (`$TopRankLabel`, `$CenterSuitLabel`) are initialized before we write to them!

## Line-by-Line Code Walkthrough

| Line | GDScript Code | Exact Meaning & Why It's Written This Way |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Line 2** | `extends Node2D` | Root script for `Table.tscn`. |
| **Line 4** | `const CardScene: PackedScene = preload("res://scenes/card/card_scene.tscn")` | Preloads our reusable card template scene at compile time. |
| **Line 6–8** | `@onready var discard_slot: Control = $DiscardSlot` | Caches references to `DiscardSlot`, `PlayerHandContainer`, and `HUD/StatusLabel`. |
| **Line 17** | `_spawn_preview_card(discard_slot, "6♥", "♥", true)` | Spawns `6♥` as the face-up starter card in the center of the table. |
| **Line 20** | `for c in starter_hand:` | Loops through our 4 initial hand dictionaries and spawns a clickable `CardScene` for each one inside `PlayerHandContainer`. |
| **Line 22** | `card_node.card_clicked.connect(_on_hand_card_clicked)` | Connects each spawned card's custom `card_clicked` signal to `Table.gd`! |

lessons.bodyMarkdown:
# Staging Cards & Playing Them onto the Center Discard Slot!

> [!TIP]
> **Tangible Milestone:** You are about to close the loop on your playable Phase 1 prototype! By the end of this lesson, you can **click one or more cards in your hand, see `Play Selected (2)` update live, and click the button to play them onto the center Discard Pile** (or click `Draw Card` to deal a new card into your hand)!

Why shouldn't clicking a card in your hand immediately throw it onto the discard pile? Because in **Kadi**, many of the most strategic moves require playing **two or more cards in a single turn**:
- Playing a **Question Card** (`Q` or `8`) accompanied by its matching **Answer Card** (`4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, A`).
- Playing multiple **Jump Cards** (`J`) or **Kickback Cards** (`K`) in a combo.
- Playing all of your remaining **Answer Cards** in one move to win after calling *"Niko Kadi!"*.

## 1. The Two-Step Staging Pattern (`staged_nodes` / `staged_cards`)

This **Select-Then-Commit** pattern is used across almost every card game, strategy game, and RPG inventory system:
1. **Step 1 — Click cards in `PlayerHandContainer` to stage/unstage them**:
   - If the clicked card is not in `staged_nodes` yet, `.append(card_node)` it, lift it `-14px` (`card_node.set_selected(true)`), and update `play_button.text = "Play Selected (%d)" % staged_nodes.size()`.
   - If it is already staged, `.erase(card_node)` it and drop it back to `0px` (`card_node.set_selected(false)`).
2. **Step 2 — Click `PlaySelectedButton` to commit the move**:
   - Clear the old card in `DiscardSlot` (`child.queue_free()`), move the newly played card visual to `DiscardSlot`, and `queue_free()` the played card nodes from `PlayerHandContainer`!

| Player Action on Screen | Signal Emitted | State Mutation in `table.gd` | Visual Result on Table |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tap un-selected card in hand** | `card_node.card_clicked(self)` | `staged_nodes.append(card_node)` | Card lifts `-14px`; button shows `Play Selected (1)` |
| **Tap already-lifted card** | `card_node.card_clicked(self)` | `staged_nodes.erase(card_node)` | Card drops to `0px`; count decreases |
| **Tap `PlaySelectedButton`** | `play_button.pressed` | Moves last staged card to `DiscardSlot`, frees staged hand nodes | Played card appears face-up in center `DiscardSlot`! |
| **Tap `DrawButton`** | `draw_button.pressed` | Instantiates a new `CardScene` into `PlayerHandContainer` | Hand fans out wider with a new clickable card! |

> [!MISTAKE]
> **Why `queue_free()` Instead of `free()`?** Never delete a Node immediately with `.free()` while a button signal or input callback is still running on it — Godot may still be processing the click event on that node! Calling `child.queue_free()` safely schedules the node for deletion at the end of the current frame.

## Line-by-Line Code Walkthrough

| Line | GDScript Code | Exact Meaning & Why It's Written This Way |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Line 10** | `var staged_nodes: Array[Control] = []` | Typed array holding the `CardScene` instances currently lifted (`-14px`) by the player. |
| **Line 13–14** | `play_button.pressed.connect(_on_play_selected_pressed)` | Connects the HUD buttons (`PlaySelectedButton` and `DrawButton`) in `_ready()`. |
| **Line 20** | `if card_node in staged_nodes:` | Checks if the tapped card is already staged so tapping again deselects it. |
| **Line 30** | `func _on_play_selected_pressed() -> void:` | Commits all staged cards when the player clicks **Play Selected**. |
| **Line 35** | `for old_child in discard_slot.get_children(): old_child.queue_free()` | Clears the previous card visual from `DiscardSlot` before displaying the newly played top card. |

The **Two-Step Staging Pattern** (select items into a staging array, then commit on action) powers:
- **Tactical RPGs (Into the Breach / Fire Emblem)**: Click unit -> highlight movement path (`staged_tile`) -> click Confirm to move.

debugChallenge.bugDescription: When you deal a match of Kadi, players notice there are ZERO Aces anywhere in the deck, and `new_deck.size()` prints 50 instead of 54!
debugChallenge.explanation: In GDScript, the second argument of `range(start, end)` is **exclusive**. Because Ace is rank `14`, writing `range(2, 14)` on line 4 stopped at `13` (King) and omitted all 4 Aces! Changing line 4 to `range(2, 15)` includes `14` and restores all 54 cards.
debugChallenge.hint: Check the inner `for rank in range(...)` loop on line 4: remember that `range(start, end)` stops at `end - 1`!
